output.brief:
The evidence doesn't show that store 14's losses have really risen. The Q1–Q3 figures are estimates extrapolated from partial counts. Their margin of error is about ±0.6 points per quarter, and the rise is 0.8 points. Across the chain, about half of the stores with two consecutive rises of this size were not confirmed by the year-end count. Store 14's full-count shrink has stayed at 1.5–1.8% for three years. The shoplifting log rise is probably an app effect. The incident app launched chain-wide on 1 April, and recorded incidents roughly doubled at the average store while chain shrink stayed flat. The self-checkout and bus-interchange explanations fit the timing but have no test separating them from estimate noise. The sales mix hasn't changed, so that explanation is out. The ethics-line tip was checked against CCTV and found unsubstantiated, so it gives no basis for acting against the stocker.

Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December full count and refuse the proposal to drop it. Hold off on a guard, removing or staffing the lanes, and any action against the stocker until the count result is compared with the estimates. Then decide based on that result. I'm fairly confident in this, but I didn't test the individual causes, so those remain open.
